Zod ^4.4.3 — existing schemas use z.object().safeParse(); new schema follows same pattern
bcrypt ^5.1.1 — bcrypt.compare and bcrypt.hash already used in authService.ts
jsonwebtoken ^9.0.2 — requireJwt populates req.user = { userId, email, username }
better-sqlite3 ^12.11.1 — synchronous prepared statements, no ORM; db singleton from db/client.ts

features: Existing routes: POST /api/auth/register, POST /api/auth/login, GET /api/auth/me (requireJwt-guarded) — mounted at /api/auth in app.ts
requireJwt (middleware/requireJwt.ts): reads Authorization Bearer header, verifies with JWT_SECRET, sets req.user = { userId, email, username }, calls next(new AuthError) on failure

GET /api/auth/me in authController.ts uses req.user.userId exclusively (line 38: authService.getById(req.user.userId)); no URL param or query param handling exists — requirement 9 is already satisfied, no code change needed
Error classes in errors/index.ts: ValidationError (400), ConflictError (409), AuthError (401), DatabaseError (500) — all reusable; no new classes needed
Users table columns: id TEXT PK, email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, username TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, password TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT datetime('now')
authService.ts has toUserResponse helper returning { id, email, username, createdAt } — same shape required for PATCH response
No /api/users route exists in app.ts; no userRoutes, userController, userService, or userSchema files exist yet
architecture: Layer order: routes/ (HTTP method + path + middleware application) → controllers/ (body parsing + schema validation + response) → services/ (business logic + DB calls) → db/client.ts (better-sqlite3 singleton)
Controllers call schema.safeParse(req.body) and throw ValidationError on failure; services are not responsible for input validation
Services execute all DB work via db.prepare('SQL').get()/run() with positional ? placeholders — synchronous, no ORM
app.ts mounts routers with app.use(prefix, router); 404 catch-all is at line 28 — new router must be inserted before it at approximately line 27
File naming: camelCase with domain prefix + layer suffix (userRoutes.ts, userController.ts, userService.ts, userSchema.ts)
New files: src/routes/userRoutes.ts, src/controllers/userController.ts, src/services/userService.ts, src/schemas/userSchema.ts
edgeCases: Empty body or body with only unrecognised fields → 400: Zod schema must require at least one of { username, email, newPassword } to be present (superRefine or .refine())
newPassword present without currentPassword → 400: Zod schema refinement must catch this combination
currentPassword present alone (no newPassword, no other updatable fields) → 400: falls under the empty/no-recognised-field rule since currentPassword alone is not a writable field
Wrong currentPassword → 400 with exact JSON { error: 'Current password is incorrect' } — not a generic ValidationError message; must match exactly
Self-collision: updating email or username to the caller's own current value must NOT return 409; uniqueness SQL must scope to WHERE (email = ? OR username = ?) AND id != ? (exclude caller's own row)
Atomicity: check email uniqueness, then username uniqueness, then (and only then) execute UPDATE — a conflict on either field must prevent any write; no partial updates
Simultaneous username rename + conflicting email in same request body → 409, neither field written (tested by requirement 7 atomicity check)
bcrypt hash storage: newPassword must be hashed with bcrypt.hash() before UPDATE; stored value must match /^\$2[aby]?\$/ and must not equal the plaintext string
Response shape: { user: { id, email, username, createdAt } } — password field must be absent from every successful response
Expired or tampered JWT → 401: handled by requireJwt before controller; no controller-level auth handling needed
GET /api/auth/me with ?id=X&userId=X query params: controller already ignores query params (uses only req.user.userId) — no code change required

tasks.description: Create src/services/userService.ts with an updateUser(userId: string, data: { username?: string; email?: string; currentPassword?: string; newPassword?: string }) function. Implementation order: (1) if newPassword provided, fetch user row by userId, bcrypt.compare(currentPassword, row.password) — throw new ValidationError('Current password is incorrect') on mismatch; (2) if email provided, query SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ? AND id != ? — throw new ConflictError() if a row is found; (3) if username provided, query SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = ? AND id != ? — throw new ConflictError() if a row is found; (4) if newPassword provided, hash it with bcrypt.hash(newPassword, 10); (5) build and execute a single UPDATE users SET ... WHERE id = ? covering only the supplied fields; (6) fetch and return the updated row via a toUserResponse-style helper that returns { id, email, username, createdAt } without password.
